receipts.leaks: The light-wallet server learns your IP address. The query carries no address, amount or transaction.

Nothing over the network: this runs offline. But the URI itself is the leak surface. Anyone you hand it to sees the address, the amount and the memo, and a memo is readable by every holder of the viewing key, so put an opaque order id there and not a customer's name.

receipts.detail: No sealed txid yet. Set ZCASH_NOW_SEALED_TXID to the txid of a shielded payment approved in a wallet. This recipe is human-gated: Noir Wallet requires approval, so it cannot run on a schedule.
receipts.leaks: The light-wallet server learns your IP address and exactly which transaction you care about. That is a real disclosure, and it is why this goes to a light-wallet server over TLS instead of to a third-party explorer: one party instead of two. Routing it through Nym would remove the IP, and has not been done yet.

receipts.detail: No sealed txid yet. Set ZCASH_NOW_SEALED_TXID to the txid of a shielded payment approved in a wallet. This recipe is human-gated: Noir Wallet requires approval, so it cannot run on a schedule.
receipts.leaks: On chain: nothing about amount, sender or receiver, which is the point of a shielded payment. Off chain: the wallet's own light-wallet server sees your IP and the moment you broadcast, which is a timing signal. The memo is readable by every holder of the viewing key. And once the txid is published as a receipt here, this particular payment is publicly linked to this project, which is a disclosure we chose to make and would not make with a real user's payment.
